TestEeprom decompilation analysis
==================================
Ghidra address: 01d44010 (ELF VA: 0x1c44010)
Source: LogicProfessionalDevice.cpp line 0x54 (84)

Callers: Only via vtable (3 vtable entries at 0x018413ec, 0x01a9a9e8, 0x0040308c)
Not called during normal init -- called on demand through device interface.

Algorithm (reconstructed from decompilation):
----------------------------------------------

1. WRITE PHASE: Write test pattern to EEPROM addresses 0x0008..0x0FFF
   - Builds a std::vector<u8> for each 256-byte chunk
   - Loop: for address = 8; address < 0x1000; address += 0x100
     - Fill buffer with incrementing byte pattern starting from a counter
     - Counter starts at 0, increments per byte written, wraps at 256
     - Last chunk (starting at 0x0F00) is only 0x100 bytes (256 - 8 for the gap)
     - Actually: the loop adjusts buffer size when address + 0x100 > 0x1000
   - Calls WriteEeprom(this->device_features, address, &buffer) via vtable[0x10]
   - Start address = 8 (skips first 8 bytes = "CY" bootloader header + VID/PID)
   - sVar7 = starting address (starts at 8, increments by 0x100)

2. READ PHASE: Read back entire EEPROM (0x000..0xFFF) via ReadEeprom
   - Calls FUN_01d43660(result_vec, this) = ReadEeprom
   - ReadEeprom reads 16 chunks of 0x100 bytes at offsets 0x0000..0x0F00
   - Returns a vector of 0x1000 (4096) bytes total
   - Uses vtable[0x18] = ReadEeprom(device_features, offset, buffer, 0x100)

3. VERIFY PHASE: Check bytes starting at offset 8
   - If total length < 9, skip verification (empty EEPROM)
   - Loop: for i = 0; i < (total_length - 8); i++
     - Expected: (char)i  (incrementing pattern 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, ... wrapping at 256)
     - Actual: data[8 + i]
     - If mismatch: assert("false", "EEprom error detected!") -- FATAL ERROR
   - Key: verification starts at byte index 8 (after the CY+VID/PID header)

4. CLEANUP: Free allocated buffers

Key observations:
-----------------
- EEPROM size = 4096 bytes (0x1000) for FX3 Pro devices
- First 8 bytes (0x0000-0x0007) are PRESERVED (not overwritten):
  - 0x0000-0x0001: "CY" magic
  - 0x0002-0x0003: B2 bootloader header
  - 0x0004-0x0007: VID/PID (little-endian)
- Test pattern: simple incrementing counter 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, ... wrapping
- Self-test is DESTRUCTIVE: overwrites all EEPROM data from byte 8 onward
  (device ID, calibration coefficients, hardware revision -- all destroyed!)
- This is a manufacturing/diagnostic test, NOT safe for production use
- After TestEeprom, the device needs recalibration/reprogramming

EEPROM Layout refresher (from memory):
- 0x0000: "CY" + B2 bootloader header (4 bytes)
- 0x0004: VID/PID (4 bytes)
- 0x0008: Device serial/ID (8 bytes) -- OVERWRITTEN BY TEST
- 0x0010: 16 calibration coefficients (16 bytes) -- OVERWRITTEN BY TEST
- 0x0020: "REV" + hw revision (6 bytes) -- OVERWRITTEN BY TEST
- 0x0026-0x01FF: 0xFF padding -- OVERWRITTEN BY TEST
- 0x0200-0x0FFF: unknown/unused -- OVERWRITTEN BY TEST

ReadEeprom (FUN_01d43660):
- Uses vtable[0x18] = ReadEeprom(device_features, offset, buffer, count)
- Reads 16 x 256-byte chunks at offsets 0x0000..0x0F00
- Concatenates into single 4096-byte vector
- This is the FX3 ReadEeprom that uses EP1 ReadVersion(0x07) I2C tunnel

WriteEeprom:
- Uses vtable[0x10] = WriteEeprom(device_features, address, &buffer)
- Writes chunks of up to 256 bytes

WipeEeprom (FUN_01d50820):
- Allocates 0x26 (38) bytes, fills with 0xFF
- Calls WriteEeprom(device_features, 0, &buffer)
- This wipes the first 38 bytes of EEPROM
- Also preserves nothing -- wipes CY header too!
